topline.text: Another quiet 24-48 hours nationally - no new DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, SEND or funding announcement cleared the corroboration bar, so today's edition stays short rather than padded.

Locally, the Talbot Specialist School dispute (the Norton Lees SEND school maintained by Sheffield City Council) remains unresolved, with the NEU's six called strike days continuing through the month.
topline.action: Keep an eye on further strike days this month if you route SEND placements or respite support through Talbot.

topline.text: Reminder: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform closes in 7 days, on 19 November.

diary.text: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 - 'Break the Silence' theme; Odd Socks Day opens the week on 16 Nov.
DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes - 7 days away.
Deadline for every mainstream school in England to publish its first statutory inclusion strategy statement.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: Talbot dispute still unresolved as strike days continue.
items.body: The NEU's dispute with Sheffield City Council over workload, safe working practices and governance at Talbot Specialist School remains unresolved more than a week after the first walkout on 5 November; the union has called six strike days across the month in total, and no settlement has been reported.
items.action: Worth flagging to any mainstream colleagues who route SEND placements or respite support through Talbot, in case further strike days this month disrupt provision.

box.label: Jargon-buster - inclusion strategy statement
box.intro: A new statutory duty landing on every mainstream school in England.
box.text: By 31 December 2026, schools must publish a short (around 500-word) statement on their website setting out what they're doing - and spending, including any Inclusive Mainstream Fund money - to remove barriers to learning and participation. DfE issued a template in June; statements must be reviewed annually.
